Group by rental.staff_id (the staff who handled the rental) instead of payment.staff_id, using payments joined to rentals. Return that staff_id, SUM(payment.amount), and the fraction of the total.

Include only staff who appear in rental-linked payments.

Group by payment.staff_id with the fraction taken against the total of all payments, where the numerator is limited to rental-linked payments (this differs from the existing interpretations only in how the denominator is scoped).
Treat "links to a rental" as the payment's rental_id matching a rental row, and also require that rental to have a non-NULL return_date.

Group by the staff member who handled the rental (rental.staff_id), but take the total from payments and compute the fraction against the rental-linked total, so the rental-handler grouping is paired with the linked-only denominator.
Return the fraction as a separate window-function column (SUM(amount) OVER ()), so each staff row carries the grand total alongside its share.
Count each rental's payments only once, so rentals with multiple payments are de-duplicated before summing.
Show staff names alongside the staff ID.
queries:
SELECT staff_id, SUM(amount), SUM(amount) * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(amount) FROM payment WHERE rental_id IS NOT NULL)
FROM payment
WHERE rental_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY staff_id

SELECT p.staff_id, SUM(p.amount) AS total_amount, SUM(p.amount) * 1.0 / SUM(SUM(p.amount)) OVER () AS fraction_of_total
FROM payment p
JOIN rental r ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id
GROUP BY p.staff_id

SELECT r.staff_id, SUM(p.amount) AS total_amount, SUM(p.amount) * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(p2.amount) FROM payment p2 JOIN rental r2 ON p2.rental_id = r2.rental_id) AS fraction
FROM payment p
JOIN rental r ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id
GROUP BY r.staff_id;

SELECT staff_id, SUM(amount) * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(amount) FROM payment WHERE rental_id IS NOT NULL) AS fraction
FROM payment
WHERE rental_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY staff_id

SELECT c.name, SUM(p.amount) * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(amount) FROM payment) AS fraction
FROM payment p
JOIN rental r ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id
JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
JOIN film_category fc ON i.film_id = fc.film_id
JOIN category c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id
GROUP BY c.name;
